correctness.rationale: For finite simple H with at least one edge and positive integral cluster sizes, finite-group Fourier positivity gives all cut inequalities. The t>0 normalization is legitimate for supremum (f=delta_0 gives t=1); random signed cuts with the empty cut imply W<2. Both directions of sigma(H(n))=sigma(H) follow from Bernoulli-cut lifting and cluster-permutation symmetrization / whole-cluster projection. Symmetry of K_r, m=r(r-1)/2 and maxcut=floor(r^2/4), gives a=1/floor(r/2) and tau=2ceil(r/2), including r=2 and both parities. Exact independent Fourier and signed lift checks corroborate; finite experiments do not prove the universal statement.

final_claim.scope: All finite simple graphs with at least one edge; all positive integral independent-vertex blowups; no arbitrary graph substitutions or all-extremizer classification.
final_claim.statement: For each finite simple graph H with at least one edge and each positive integer vector n, tau(H(n))=tau(H), where tau is the normalized positive-definite Fourier edge-shell Turán mass on the Boolean vertex group. Hence tau(K_(n1,...,nr))=2 ceil(r/2) for r>=2.
